result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.bridging_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute bridging centrality for each node. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20762-L20845){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.bridging_centrality( normalized=True, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bridging centrality](/assets/graphs/bridging-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph shaded by bridging centrality, betweenness weighted by how much a node links otherwise separate parts. Bridge node E scores 1.00 after normalizing, the tail node F 0.76 and the hub C only 0.34, while A and G score 0." width="100%"} Bridging centrality identifies nodes that act as bridges between densely connected communities. It combines the *bridging coefficient* (a local measure of how much a node links to otherwise-separated groups) with *betweenness centrality* (global importance for shortest paths): $$\mathrm{BrC}(v) = \mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{coeff}}(v) \times \mathrm{betweenness}(v)$$ where the bridging coefficient is: $$\mathrm{BC}_{\mathrm{coeff}}(v) = \frac{1/d(v)}{\sum_{j \in N(v)} 1/d(j)}$$ ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [normalized]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (the default), normalize so the maximum value is `1.0`. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name for the node attribute to store results. If not provided, defaults to `"bridging_centrality"`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the raw dictionary. If `False`, store as node attributes and return self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to bridging centrality scores. Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In a barbell graph (two cliques joined by a single bridge), the bridge node scores highest: ::: {#fd79bff7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=False) for i in range(1, 5): g.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(5, 9): g.add_node(label=str(i)) # Clique 1 for i in range(1, 5): for j in range(i + 1, 5): g.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) # Clique 2 for i in range(5, 9): for j in range(i + 1, 9): g.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) # Bridge g.add_edge("4", "5") g.bridging_centrality(return_dict=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {7: 0.0, 3: 0.0, 6: 0.0, 2: 0.0, 5: 1.0, 1: 0.0, 8: 0.0, 4: 1.0} ``` ::: :::
